newsitem.title: CROATIA: Merrill Lynch sees Croatia investment grade rating.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch sees Croatia investment grade rating.

text.p: Merrill Lynch, one of Croatia's two credit rating advisors, said on Wednesday it was fairly confident the country would be awarded an investment grade rating vital for its future debt issues.
"It is difficult to be absolutely sure with these things and if something goes wrong, then it might not be achieved," vice president of Merrill Lynch International, Pascal Najadi, told Reuters.
Three leading international agencies are expected to pass their rating assessment by mid-January.
Apart from encouraging figures, Najadi said Croatia's European orientation, mentality of the people and skilled workforce singled it out among other emerging countries.
"For me, Croatia is not an emerging market, it is a Central European state. I compare it to Switzerland," he added.
Together with a local Zagrebacka Banka, Merrill led a 300-kuna maiden issue of two-year Eurokuna the government has just launched at home and abroad.
It was also hired to manage the first dollar-denominated Eurobonds the former Yugoslav republic plans to issue early next year after getting the rating.
The authorities hope to secure a BBB rating to attract large institutional investors, but have said they will not be too disappointed even if Croatia is initially rated BB+.

But some analysts suspect a shaky political situation in the country and vicinity of the trouled Bosnia might spoil the chances offered by an otherwise solid economic performance. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
